findings.evidence: Mathlib `BorelSpace/Basic.lean:395` `secondCountableTopologyEither_of_left ... [SecondCountableTopology α] : SecondCountableTopologyEither α β`; `:614` `ContinuousSMul.measurableSMul₂ ... [SecondCountableTopologyEither M α] ... : MeasurableSMul₂ M α`.
findings.fix: Drop the binder: `[NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] {lam ρ : Measure X} [SigmaFinite lam]`.
findings.issue: `[SecondCountableTopology E]` is not needed. Measurability of `x ↦ c x • g x` only needs `MeasurableSMul₂ ℝ E`, and Mathlib derives that from `SecondCountableTopologyEither ℝ E`, which holds because ℝ is second countable. Nothing else in the proof uses second countability of `E`.

findings.evidence: The `hle` already in the diff gives `∀ᵐ x ∂ρ, ‖c x⁻¹ • g x‖ ≤ 1`, so the clipped field equals the unclipped one `ρ`-a.e. An everywhere bound implies an a.e. bound for every measure, including `lam`.
findings.fix: State `∃ σ, Measurable σ ∧ (∀ x, ‖σ x‖ ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂ρ, ...`. Take `σ x := if ‖c x⁻¹ • g x‖ ≤ 1 then c x⁻¹ • g x else 0` (measurable via `Measurable.ite` on `measurableSet_le`), and use `hle`/`heq` for the `ρ`-a.e. equality. Callers that need the `lam`-a.e. bound get it from `ae_of_all`.
findings.issue: The conclusion `∀ᵐ x ∂lam, ‖σ x‖ ≤ 1` is weaker than what can be proved. Setting `σ` to zero wherever its norm exceeds 1 gives a measurable field with norm at most 1 at every point that still agrees with the old one `ρ`-a.e. (by the PR's own `hle`). That makes the `HaveLebesgueDecomposition` case split and the singular-part argument unnecessary.

summary: Dropping `hlam` is correct, but `exists_norm_le_one_toReal_rnDeriv_smul_eq` still has an unnecessary `[SecondCountableTopology E]`. Its conclusion can also be strengthened to a pointwise bound, which makes the new Lebesgue-decomposition case split unnecessary.
